prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished, high-fidelity native Windows game-launcher concept for The Order: 1886. This is composition A, a cinematic launch bar. Render a single complete desktop app window, straight-on, landscape 3:2, crisp and readable, with no surrounding desktop or presentation-board captions.

Input image is a reference for the existing game's imagery, charcoal/brass/ivory identity, and serif wordmark only. Replace the old left-hand menu composition entirely. Keep the subject clearly recognizable: the armored protagonist and misty Victorian London street from the reference. This is an operating interface, not a poster with text.

Structure: a slim native dark Windows title bar; then a generous cinematic artwork region occupying the upper two-thirds. Set the elegant brass serif wordmark "THE ORDER" with "1886" below at the upper left, with generous breathing room. Put quiet, plainly readable "Settings", "Verify files", and "View logs" actions along the upper right. The bottom third is a single opaque charcoal launch console, anchored edge to edge, with no floating cards, glass, blur, ornamental frames or decorative gradients.

Inside the console, a wide first row shows the label "Game folder", a sober native path field displaying "…\CUSA00076", a small "Change" button, and a restrained "Game files found" status. The next row groups three native dropdowns: "Display" / "Borderless", "Upscaling" / "FSR 1", "Frame rate" / "30 FPS". Place one large, exceptionally clear matte brass "Play" button at the right of these controls. Keep the warning "Experimental runtime. Gameplay is not yet verified." readable beneath the controls. Small keyboard hint "Enter to play" can sit by the primary action.

Visual grammar: exact family of dark colors from the reference, charcoal #0b0b0a, brass #d4bd75, ivory #e9e5d8, warm muted text #a8a497. Interface typography is a highly readable Windows humanist sans, only the game wordmark is serif. Strong hierarchy and deliberate spacing, narrow quiet separators, rectangular native controls with subtly softened corners, all text accessible and legible. One focal action. Artwork is rich and cinematic; the controls are calm and practical.

Only show the real capabilities described here. Settings values are illustrative configuration, not measured performance. Do not add CPU/GPU charts, measured FPS, benchmark claims, a store, account, download manager, mod manager, or a claim that the game is playable. No numbered sections, badges above headings, fake technical metrics, large rounded card grids, extra emblems, or unrelated branding.
approval: User selected option 1 (cinematic launch bar) in chat, 2026-10-16.
